caveats: LFS and SEPH employment are different measures: do not compare their levels. The LFS is a household survey that counts employed people (a person with two jobs counts once), including the self-employed and agriculture; SEPH counts payroll jobs, so it leaves out the self-employed and agriculture, fishing and trapping, private household services, religious organisations and military personnel of the defence services. LFS estimates carry sampling error; preliminary SEPH estimates are revised. Compare trends over several months, not one month's change. For earnings in a detailed industry, such as provincial and territorial public administration (NAICS 912), use SEPH (14-10-0203 monthly, 14-10-0204 annual) and say why: the LFS wage table 14-10-0064 stops at broad sectors ('Public administration' as a whole).

LFS figures are survey estimates. Table 14-10-0287 publishes the standard error of each estimate, of its month-to-month change and of its year-over-year change (the Statistics dimension). A change is significant at the 5% level only when the change plus or minus two standard errors excludes zero, which many small monthly moves do not. Statistics Canada releases estimates with a CV up to 16.5% freely, with a warning up to 33.3%, and not above; estimates under a minimum size (1,500 for Canada) are suppressed. Seasonally adjusted series are revised once a year.

The official CPI (not seasonally adjusted, table 18-10-0004) is never revised once published. Seasonally adjusted indexes (18-10-0006) are the only CPI series revised: one month after release, and each January for the past 36 months; each is adjusted on its own, so they do not add up to the all-items index. The basket weights are updated every year since 2022.

CPI-trim and CPI-median are built from seasonally adjusted prices and are revised: since the January 2026 CPI, each January revises the past three years and every other month revises one past month. CPI-common is revised as its factor model is re-estimated on all past data. Today's value for a past month may differ from what was first published: for what was known on a date, use table 18-10-0259 (real-time releases) or wds_get_series_as_of.

Monthly GDP by industry (36-10-0434) is at basic prices; quarterly expenditure-based GDP (36-10-0104) is at market prices. They are estimated differently, so their growth rates can differ, and both are revised as new data arrive. Real values in chained (2017) dollars are not additive: components do not sum to their aggregate, and the gap grows with distance from 2017. To split growth into parts, use the 'Contributions to percent change' series of 36-10-0104 rather than adding or subtracting chained levels.

These tables classify industries by NAICS 2022 (monthly GDP by industry since its 28 November 2025 release) or occupations by NOC 2021. Series on earlier versions (NAICS 2017 and before, NOC 2016) are terminated series or separate inactive tables, such as 14-10-0296 on NOC 2016: codes do not match one for one across versions, so do not splice an old and a new series without checking the concordance.

Annual inflation for a calendar year is the change between two annual average indexes, which Statistics Canada publishes each January in table 18-10-0005-01 and computes from the published, rounded indexes. Read it there: averaging the 12 monthly values of 18-10-0004-01 yourself can differ by 0.1 point, and the December-to-December change is a different measure. Say which one you report.

Most CPI components are published for Canada and the provinces only. Mortgage interest cost is published for Canada alone: no province or city has it. For Toronto, tables 18-10-0004 and 18-10-0005 publish six series only: All-items, Shelter, Rented accommodation, Owned accommodation, Water, fuel and electricity, and All-items (1992=100). A city figure for any other component does not exist; say so and offer the national or provincial figure instead.

# ============================================================
# StatCan vectors
# Purpose: Fetch the data behind MapleStats MCP's wds_get_data_from_vectors
#          (exact: WDS vectors request from the vector ids)
# Inputs:  https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods
# Outputs: data/raw/vectors.json; the prepared table as `data`
# ============================================================

# 0. Setup ----

library(cansim)
library(dplyr)
library(janitor)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)

dir.create("data/raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# 1. Read inputs ----

data <- get_cansim_vector_for_latest_periods(
  c("v2062815", "v2062811", "v41690973", "v108785714", "v108785715", "v65201210", "v52300157", "v2132579"),
  periods = 133
)

# 2. Check inputs ----

stopifnot("https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods returned no rows" = nrow(data) > 0)

# 3. Prepare data ----

data <- data |>
  clean_names()

# cansim adds val_norm (the value times its scalar factor) and a Date column.
# Suppressed observations keep a missing val_norm, as the tool returned them.

# Standard cleaning: trimmed text, empty strings as missing, and numbers
# stored as text converted to numbers. Codes stay text as the source
# wrote them: columns named like one (coordinate, vector_id, dguid, NAICS,
# postal code) and columns with a leading zero (01, 000000001).

code_columns <- "^(coordinate|vector|vector_?id|product_?id|pid|dguid|[a-z0-9_]*_dguid|postal_?code|[a-z0-9_]*_postal_code|fsa|[a-z0-9_]*naics[a-z0-9_]*|noc|noc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_noc|sgc|sgc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_sgc)$"
data <- data |>
  mutate(across(where(is.character), \(x) na_if(str_trim(x), "")))
keep_text <- names(data)[
  str_detect(names(data), code_columns) |
    map_lgl(
      data,
      \(column) is.character(column) && any(str_detect(column, "^-?0[0-9]"), na.rm = TRUE)
    )
]
data <- data |>
  mutate(
    across(any_of(keep_text), \(x) if (is.list(x)) x else as.character(x)),
    across(where(is.character) & !any_of(keep_text), parse_guess)
  )

# ============================================================
# StatCan vectors
# Purpose: Fetch the data behind MapleStats MCP's wds_get_data_from_vectors
#          (exact: WDS vectors request from the vector ids)
# Inputs:  https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods
# Outputs: data/raw/vectors.json; the prepared table as `data`
# ============================================================

# %% 0. Setup

import json
import re
import unicodedata
from pathlib import Path

import httpx
import polars as pl

RAW_DIR = Path("data/raw")
RAW_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
raw_path = RAW_DIR / "vectors.json"

# %% 1. Read inputs

with httpx.Client(
    http2=True,
    follow_redirects=True,
    timeout=300,
    headers={"User-Agent": "MapleStats MCP reproduction script (https://github.com/dsanchezp18/maplestats-mcp)"},
) as client:
    response = client.post('https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods', json=[{'vectorId': 2062815, 'latestN': 133}, {'vectorId': 2062811, 'latestN': 133}, {'vectorId': 41690973, 'latestN': 133}, {'vectorId': 108785714, 'latestN': 133}, {'vectorId': 108785715, 'latestN': 133}, {'vectorId': 65201210, 'latestN': 133}, {'vectorId': 52300157, 'latestN': 133}, {'vectorId': 2132579, 'latestN': 133}])
response.raise_for_status()
raw_path.write_bytes(response.content)

payload = json.loads(raw_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
# One object per requested item; its rows also get the item's own
# fields (for WDS: vectorId, productId, coordinate).

records = [
    {
        **{
            key: value
            for key, value in item['object'].items()
            if not isinstance(value, (dict, list))
        },
        **row,
    }
    for item in payload
    # An item the source could not serve (a WDS FAILED vector) has no rows.
    if isinstance(item['object'], dict) and 'vectorDataPoint' in item['object']
    for row in item['object']['vectorDataPoint']
]
data = pl.json_normalize(records, strict=False)

# %% 2. Check inputs

assert data.height > 0, "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods returned no rows"

# %% 3. Prepare data

# scalarFactorCode is the value's power of ten; refPer is the reference date.

data = data.with_columns(
    (pl.col("value") * 10 ** pl.col("scalarFactorCode")).alias("value_normalized"),
    pl.col("refPer").str.to_date(strict=False).alias("ref_date"),
)

# Standard cleaning: snake_case names as janitor's clean_names() gives them
# in R (PÉRIODE -> periode, referenceNumber -> reference_number, # -> number,
# % -> percent, apostrophes dropped, a leading digit prefixed with x),
# trimmed text, empty strings as missing. Names that clean alike are
# numbered as janitor numbers them (Indicator, indicator -> indicator,
# indicator_2).

clean_names = [
    re.sub(
        r"[^0-9a-z]+",
        "_",
        re.sub(
            r"([a-z0-9])([A-Z])",
            r"\1_\2",
            "".join(
                " " if unicodedata.category(ch)[0] in "PS" and not ch.isascii() else ch
                for ch in unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", column.replace("'", ""))
            )
            .replace("#", " number ")
            .replace("%", " percent ")
            .encode("ascii", "ignore")
            .decode(),
        ).lower(),
    ).strip("_")
    or "x"
    for column in data.columns
]
clean_names = [f"x{name}" if name[0].isdigit() else name for name in clean_names]
while len(set(clean_names)) < len(clean_names):
    name_counts = {}
    numbered = []
    for name in clean_names:
        name_counts[name] = name_counts.get(name, 0) + 1
        count = name_counts[name]
        numbered.append(name if count == 1 else f"{name}_{count}")
    clean_names = numbered
data = data.rename(dict(zip(data.columns, clean_names)))
data = data.with_columns(pl.col(pl.Utf8).str.strip_chars().replace("", None))

# Numbers stored as text become numbers. Codes stay text as the source
# wrote them: columns named like one (coordinate, vector_id, dguid, NAICS,
# postal code) and columns with a leading zero (01, 000000001).

code_columns = re.compile(r"^(coordinate|vector|vector_?id|product_?id|pid|dguid|[a-z0-9_]*_dguid|postal_?code|[a-z0-9_]*_postal_code|fsa|[a-z0-9_]*naics[a-z0-9_]*|noc|noc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_noc|sgc|sgc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_sgc)$")
for column in data.columns:
    dtype = data.schema[column]
    if code_columns.search(column) and not dtype.is_nested():
        data = data.with_columns(pl.col(column).cast(pl.Utf8))
        continue
    if dtype != pl.Utf8 or data[column].null_count() == data.height:
        continue
    numbers = data[column].cast(pl.Float64, strict=False)
    leading_zero = data[column].str.contains(r"^-?0[0-9]").any()
    if numbers.null_count() > data[column].null_count() or leading_zero:
        continue
    whole = data[column].cast(pl.Int64, strict=False)
    data = data.with_columns(whole if whole.null_count() == numbers.null_count() else numbers)

* 0. Setup

capture mkdir "data"

response.raise_for_status()
raw_path.write_bytes(response.content)
payload = json.loads(raw_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
records = [{**{key: value for key, value in item['object'].items() if not isinstance(value, (dict, list))}, **row} for item in payload  if isinstance(item['object'], dict) and 'vectorDataPoint' in item['object'] for row in item['object']['vectorDataPoint']]
data = pl.json_normalize(records, strict=False)
nested = [name for name, dtype in data.schema.items() if dtype.is_nested()]
data = data.with_columns(pl.col(name).map_elements(lambda value: json.dumps(value.to_list() if isinstance(value, pl.Series) else value, default=str), return_dtype=pl.Utf8) for name in nested)
data.write_csv(RAW_DIR / "vectors_prepared.csv")
end

import delimited "data/raw/vectors_prepared.csv", clear varnames(1) encoding("utf-8") stringcols(_all) bindquote(strict) maxquotedrows(unlimited)

* 2. Check inputs

assert _N > 0

* 3. Prepare data

* scalarfactorcode is the value's power of ten.

generate double value_normalized = real(value) * 10^real(scalarfactorcode)
generate ref_date = date(refper, "YMD")
format ref_date %td

* Standard cleaning: lower-case names, trimmed text, and numbers stored as
* text converted (destring leaves genuinely non-numeric text alone). Codes
* stay text as the source wrote them: variables named like one (coordinate,
* vectorid, dguid, NAICS, postal code) and ones with a leading zero (01).
* rename *, lower stops at a clash (Indicator next to indicator), so names
* that lower-case alike are numbered as janitor numbers them (indicator,
* indicator_2), then renamed in one group rename, which allows swaps.

local names
foreach var of varlist _all {
    local names `names' `=strlower("`var'")'
}
local dups : list dups names
while "`dups'" != "" {
    local numbered
    local before
    foreach name of local names {
        local count 1
        foreach earlier of local before {
            if "`earlier'" == "`name'" local ++count
        }
        local before `before' `name'
        if `count' > 1 {
            local name = substr("`name'", 1, 32 - strlen("_`count'")) + "_`count'"
        }
        local numbered `numbered' `name'
    }
    local names `numbered'
    local dups : list dups names
}
local old_names
local new_names
local i 0
foreach var of varlist _all {
    local ++i
    local name : word `i' of `names'
    if "`name'" != "`var'" {
        local old_names `old_names' `var'
        local new_names `new_names' `name'
    }
}
if "`old_names'" != "" {
    rename (`old_names') (`new_names')
}
quietly ds, has(type string)
local text_vars `r(varlist)'
foreach var of local text_vars {
    replace `var' = strtrim(`var')
    if regexm("`var'|", "^(coordinate|vector|vector_?id|product_?id|pid|dguid|[a-z0-9_]*_dguid|postal_?code|[a-z0-9_]*_postal_code|fsa|[a-z0-9_]*naics[a-z0-9_]*|noc|noc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_noc|sgc|sgc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_sgc)[|]") continue
    quietly count if regexm(`var', "^-?0[0-9]")
    if r(N) > 0 continue
    destring `var', replace
}

log close

# ============================================================
# StatCan vectors
# Purpose: Fetch the data behind MapleStats MCP's wds_get_data_from_vectors
#          (exact: WDS vectors request from the vector ids)
# Inputs:  https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods
# Outputs: data/raw/vectors.json; the prepared table as `data`
# ============================================================

# 0. Setup

using DataFrames
using Downloads
using JSON3
using Tables
using TidierData

mkpath("data/raw")

# 1. Read inputs

Downloads.request(
    "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods";
    headers = ["Content-Type" => "application/json"], method = "POST", input = IOBuffer("[{\"vectorId\": 2062815, \"latestN\": 133}, {\"vectorId\": 2062811, \"latestN\": 133}, {\"vectorId\": 41690973, \"latestN\": 133}, {\"vectorId\": 108785714, \"latestN\": 133}, {\"vectorId\": 108785715, \"latestN\": 133}, {\"vectorId\": 65201210, \"latestN\": 133}, {\"vectorId\": 52300157, \"latestN\": 133}, {\"vectorId\": 2132579, \"latestN\": 133}]"),
    output = "data/raw/vectors.json",
)
payload = JSON3.read(read("data/raw/vectors.json", String))
# One object per requested item; its rows also get the item's own
# fields (for WDS: vectorId, productId, coordinate).

records = [
    merge(
        Dict(k => v for (k, v) in item["object"] if !(v isa JSON3.Object || v isa JSON3.Array)),
        Dict(row),
    )
    # An item the source could not serve (a WDS FAILED vector) has no rows.
    for item in filter(
        i -> i["object"] isa JSON3.Object && haskey(i["object"], "vectorDataPoint"),
        payload,
    )
    for row in item["object"]["vectorDataPoint"]
]
data = DataFrame(Tables.dictrowtable(records))
data = mapcols(col -> [x === nothing ? missing : x for x in col], data)

# 2. Check inputs

@assert nrow(data) > 0 "https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest/getDataFromVectorsAndLatestNPeriods returned no rows"

# 3. Prepare data

# scalarFactorCode is the value's power of ten.

data.value_normalized = data.value .* 10.0 .^ data.scalarFactorCode

# Standard cleaning: snake_case names, trimmed text, empty strings as missing.

data = @chain data begin
    @clean_names
end
data = mapcols(
    col -> eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, AbstractString} ?
        [ismissing(x) || isempty(strip(x)) ? missing : strip(x) for x in col] : col,
    data,
)

# Numbers stored as text become numbers. Codes stay text as the source
# wrote them: columns named like one (coordinate, vector_id, dguid, NAICS,
# postal code) and columns with a leading zero (01, 000000001).

code_columns = r"^(coordinate|vector|vector_?id|product_?id|pid|dguid|[a-z0-9_]*_dguid|postal_?code|[a-z0-9_]*_postal_code|fsa|[a-z0-9_]*naics[a-z0-9_]*|noc|noc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_noc|sgc|sgc_[a-z0-9_]*|[a-z0-9_]*_sgc)$"
for name in names(data)
    column = data[!, name]
    if occursin(code_columns, name)
        data[!, name] = [ismissing(x) ? missing : string(x) for x in column]
        continue
    end
    eltype(column) <: Union{Missing, AbstractString} || continue
    values = collect(skipmissing(column))
    (isempty(values) || any(v -> occursin(r"^-?0[0-9]", v), values)) && continue
    any(v -> isnothing(tryparse(Float64, v)), values) && continue
    whole = all(v -> !isnothing(tryparse(Int, v)), values)
    data[!, name] = [
        ismissing(x) ? missing : parse(whole ? Int : Float64, x) for x in column
    ]
end
